video_title: #1 TOP Ladder Push with Log Bait 🌎🏆

tesla: Opponent card, all game (arena tracks at [7, 19], [8, 20], [2, 16], [9, 16], [8, 16]; tesla-evolution detected at t=874). Ryley names the archetype off it at t=802-806: "This guy's actually a log bait Tesla player... he's actually very good at log bait Tesla." He tracks the Evo Tesla's timing as an elixir tell - "he goes for the Evo Tesla late cuz he didn't have the elixir right away. And we just get a bunch of damage, man" (t=871-876) - and plays his Magic Archer low to dodge it: "He might go for a high middle evo Tesla to predict my magic archer" (t=967-971).
the-log: Opponent card. Ryley frames his own deck's weakness around not having one: "we do have a very difficult time dealing with uh some of his stuff like, you know, goblins, princess being low cuz we don't have like a log or anything like that. So, we have to be very very cautious" (t=833-840). He also plays his spirits around a predicted Log - "He might log predict us. No, he doesn't. That's good, dude" (t=1027-1031) - and reads a wasted one in overtime: "Bad log as well" (t=986).
goblins: Opponent card (deploy label 'GobliN3' at t=914.9, arena tracks at [11, 21], [1, 15]). Named as one of the two cards his no-Log list struggles with - "goblins, princess being low cuz we don't have like a log or anything like that" (t=835-838). He answers them by predicting: "then we fire spirit predict the goblins. Nice" (t=920-922), and calls a misplayed set from the opponent - "bad goblins by him as well" (t=1045).
princess: Opponent card, present in both lanes for most of the game (arena tracks at [13, 19], [4, 21], [7, 20], [16, 15], [12, 17]). Ryley names her as a problem card for a Log-less bait deck (t=835-838) and uses the Bomb Tower's placement to shut the lane off - "us going for this bomb tower is also going to prevent him from going for any princesses on the right side, which is very good" (t=908-911). The finishing Magic Archer is aimed through her: "Just march on the princess and this is game over, man" (t=1077).
knight: Opponent card, the mini-tank in front of every push (arena tracks at [15, 22] -> [15, 17] at t=934-938, [3, 12] in the left lane at t=876-880, [14, 13] at t=1045). Ryley answers it with Berserker at the bridge - "we can go for the knight at the I mean the berserker to keep the knight at the bridge" (t=867) - and later uses it as an alignment target for the Magic Archer: "This should line up with the knight. Keep it in line" (t=1038-1040). He talks about the opponent's ability being paired with it ("He has to go for the ability plus knight", t=932), which suggests a Hero Knight, though the ability is never named.
little-prince: Opponent card (arena track at [5, 17] at t=1001). Killed early by Ryley's Magic Archer on his own bank: "Oh, nice magic archer timing, actually. Grabbing our two shots and fully taking out that prince" (t=816-819), and later he holds an Ice Spirit specifically for it - "I have the ice spirit ready here for the potential prince at the bridge" (t=876-880).
electro-spirit: Opponent card (arena track at [6, 4] at t=1020). It shapes Ryley's biggest decision of the first half: he passes on Magic Archer chip damage rather than let the opponent activate his own King Tower - "I didn't want to give him an opportunity to activate the king tower. That's why I think that he put it on that tile cuz if I marcher here, then he can activate king with the E spirit" (t=850-856). He also predicts the Evo Tesla defence pairing - "he's going to e spirit plus log, but that's all right with me" (t=917-918) - and calls a wasted one in overtime: "bad e spirit" (t=987).

bullets: Game 5 of 7 of the session and the only one to reach overtime (video 801-1096 s); Ryley wins it on a Magic Archer grind after regulation ends 0-0, against a Log Bait Tesla mirror-ish list (Evo Tesla, Evo Goblin Barrel, Princess, Goblins, The Log, Knight, Little Prince, Electro Spirit).

The deck's plan is stated as a single matchup read: "we have to try to abuse the fact that he has a hard time dealing with magic archer" (t=827), balanced against its own hole - "we do have a very difficult time dealing with uh some of his stuff like, you know, goblins, princess being low cuz we don't have like a log or anything like that" (t=833-838).

Offence is always a package, never a single card: Fire Spirit + Goblin Barrel + Evo Wall Breakers + Magic Archer at clock 1:57-1:46 takes the enemy left tower 4400 -> 2697 HP (t=856-872), and the same shape recurs at clock 0:56-0:43 in the right lane (Goblin Barrel [14, 26], Wall Breakers [14, 14], Fire Spirit, Berserker) for 4298 -> 3178 HP.

Defence is Bomb Tower in the centre column ([9, 9], [9, 10], [8, 10], high at [9, 13]) plus Royal Delivery held for the Evolved Goblin Barrel, with Ice Spirit / Fire Spirit / Berserker as the cheap layers - "I do have to be careful though of the evo barrel. We have the delivery ready" (t=940-942), "Beautiful defense. Very clean" (t=948).

Two-lane pressure is used explicitly as an elixir tax in overtime: "we can go for the evo barrel plus evo wall breakers and he's going to have to use extra elixir on the Tesla but he's also going to have to defend the opposite lane" (t=989-995).

The two evolution slots in play are Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers ("I'm going to evo wall breakers", t=861; "the evo barrel plus evo wall breakers", t=989; wall-breaker-evolution detected on the field at t=994).

new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers as paired win conditions with spirits and small ground troops behind them is a spell-bait shell, and at 2.5 average elixir it cycles like a cycle deck.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Two 2-3 elixir win conditions (Evolved Goblin Barrel and Evolved Wall Breakers) mean the opponent must answer both lanes with spells and swarms he cannot afford to hold at once, while a 2.5 average cost lets Ryley re-present them faster than the answers cycle. Magic Archer is the reason the deck can win from behind: played from his own bank his piercing arrow reaches the enemy Crown Tower, so chip accumulates even in turns where he is purely defending, and he places it against the opponent's predicted spell rather than for maximum value ("I'm going to march her off to the side though cuz he's going to try to predict it", t=1016). Defensively it leans on a centre Bomb Tower plus a Royal Delivery held specifically for the enemy Evolved Goblin Barrel, with Ice Spirit, Fire Spirit and Berserker as the one- and two-elixir layers. The weakness Ryley names himself is the lack of a Log: Goblins and a low Princess have to be handled with predictions and bodies instead (t=833-840).
